messages:
Lena (Design): quick design check — thinking about a compact p95 "rail" for the latency card. goal: keep card height ~120px for dashboards while still surfacing p50/p95/p99 comparisons and a tiny heatmap on hover. thoughts?
Sam (PM): +1 on compacting. main ask: customers need to spot regressions at a glance. default view should surface p95 and trend; extras can be in hover/expand. also: product wants an ops-friendly copy when sampling is on.
Devon (Eng): hmm doable but two constraints: 1) computing percentiles for many series at high cardinality is expensive, 2) heatmap needs histogram bins (we don't currently expose histograms for every route). could do approximate percentiles from sketches or pre-aggregated histograms.
Ravi (Data): yep — we can serve approximate p95 from t-digest sketches. API shape suggestion: `GET /metrics/latency?window=1h&percentiles=50,95,99&approx=true` returns `p95_estimate` + `confidence`. maybe the UI shows a small `~` badge when approximate.
Maya (Accessibility): a few a11y nits: 
- tiny sparklines + color-only diff are problematic for low-vision / colorblind. add a patterned fill or explicit label on hover.
- ensure keyboard focus reveals the histogram/tooltip and that hover-only info is accessible via keyboard.
- contrast for the p95 number needs to hit 4.5:1 if it's the main stat.
Lena (Design): good points. initial mock idea: two variants —
1) single-number + micro-sparkline (p95 shown large, p50/p99 toggles in a tiny overflow menu)
2) stacked micro-rail: three horizontal mini-bars (p50/p95/p99) each with a 1-line sparkline, slightly taller but still compact.
Which gets the tradeoffs: variant 1 small footprint + faster glance; variant 2 more explicit distribution cues.
Sam (PM): variant 1 probably better for default. variant 2 could be an expanded mode or part of exploration panel. also: copy for sampling warning — propose: "Numbers shown are sampled (approx. 10% of requests). Toggle sampling for exact counts."
Ravi (Data): suggest copy tweak: "Approximate values from a sampled dataset (10%). Disable sampling to compute exact aggregations — may increase query cost." keep it short in-card, link to docs for cost implications.
Devon (Eng): technically if they disable sampling we should warn about latency explosion on the query side. maybe an interstitial: "Running exact aggregation may take 10-30s and increase cost" with a confirm.
Maya (Accessibility): for the tiny heatmap on hover, ensure cell size is >= 8px and provide alt text for the chart for screen readers: e.g., "Latency histogram: most requests between 10–50ms; tail at 700ms" (generated by backend summary).
Lena (Design): UX micro-copy suggestions then: in-card badge small: `~` with `aria-label="Approximate values (sampling enabled)"`, tooltip copy: "Approx values from 10% sampling — click for exact".
Sam (PM): can we add a lightweight CTA to open a timeline with full histogram and raw examples? customer feedback shows they want to jump to raw traces from the latency card.
Devon (Eng): we can add a link to the traces page `?route=...&time=...` — backend already supports linking by time window. only caveat: need consistent sampling param in the link.
Lena (Design): accessibility + eng constraints noted. I'll mock both variants and include keyboard flows and microcopy. will add a11y annotations and a proposed confirm dialog for "disable sampling".
deploy-bot: deploy v2-latency-rail-preview launched to staging.
Sam (PM): sweet — can design drop updated screens before the noon sync? if not, we'll review staging after deploy.
Lena (Design): yep, aiming for two mocks in Figma by 11:30. I'll post the link here when ready. :eyes:
